item.title: Four Corrections officers suspended over alleged inmate assault
item.description: The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has suspended four officers pending the outcome of an investigation into an alleged assault on an inmate at the Lautoka Remand Centre. The decision follows the circulation of CCTV footage on social media showing a prison officer allegedly dragging, punching and kicking an inmate inside the facility.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has suspended four officers pending the outcome of an investigation into an alleged assault on an inmate at the Lautoka Remand Centre.

The decision follows the circulation of CCTV footage on social media showing a prison officer allegedly dragging, punching and kicking an inmate inside the facility.

In a statement, the FCS said the suspension of staff is standard procedure when investigating allegations of assault or breaches of internal operational instructions at correctional centres.

“The Fiji Corrections Service has suspended four officers to allow for a thorough investigation into the recent incident at the Lautoka Remand Centre,” the statement said.

The footage, dated June 14 this year, has sparked widespread public concern over the conduct of prison officers and the treatment of inmates in Fiji’s correctional facilities.

The FCS confirmed that a formal investigation is underway to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The matter has also drawn the attention of the Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission, which has called for a prompt, independent and transparent investigation while reiterating that there must be zero tolerance for torture and all forms of ill-treatment in places of detention.

item.title: Fiji among countries facing new permanent US visa bond requirement
item.description: Fiji has been included in a new United States visa bond programme that will require Fijian travellers to pay a bond of up to US$20,000 (about FJ$44,000) before being issued a visitor visa. The new rule, announced by the US State Department, makes permanent a visa bond programme aimed at reducing visa overstays.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji has been included in a new United States visa bond programme that will require Fijian travellers to pay a bond of up to US$20,000 (about FJ$44,000) before being issued a visitor visa.

The new rule, announced by the US State Department, makes permanent a visa bond programme aimed at reducing visa overstays.

It comes into effect on August 3, with Fiji listed among 50 countries whose nationals may be subject to the requirement. The programme is scheduled to apply to Fiji from January 21, 2026.

The policy applies to B1 (business) and B2 (tourism) visas. Under the rule, US consular officers may require applicants from designated countries to post a refundable bond of up to US$20,000 as a condition of receiving a visa.

The State Department said the decision follows a pilot programme launched in 2025, which concluded that visa bonds were an effective tool for encouraging compliance with visa conditions and reducing overstays.

During the pilot phase, applicants could be required to pay bonds of US$5,000, US$10,000 or US$15,000. Under the permanent programme, the minimum bond has increased to US$10,000, while the maximum has been raised to US$20,000.

Fiji is one of several Pacific nations included in the programme, alongside Papua New Guinea, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu.

The State Department has not indicated that every applicant from the listed countries will automatically be required to pay a bond. Instead, the decision will be made on a case-by-case basis by consular officers during the visa application process.

US officials say the policy is designed to reduce visa overstays and strengthen immigration compliance.

However, immigration and civil rights advocates have criticised the measure, arguing it could discourage legitimate travel and create additional financial barriers for visitors from affected countries.

The new rule is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register on August 3, formally bringing the programme into effect.

item.title: New Sanatan body launched in Fiji
item.description: A new Hindu religious organisation, the Sanatan Dharm Fiji Sabha, has been officially inaugurated, becoming the second national Sanatan body in Fiji alongside the long-established Shree Sanatan Dharm Pratinidhi Sabha of Fiji. The inaugural ceremony was held yesterday at the Kings Complex in Nausori and was attended by the High Commissioner of India to Fiji, Suneet Mehta, who officially launched th
item.content:encoded:
A new Hindu religious organisation, the Sanatan Dharm Fiji Sabha, has been officially inaugurated, becoming the second national Sanatan body in Fiji alongside the long-established Shree Sanatan Dharm Pratinidhi Sabha of Fiji.

The inaugural ceremony was held yesterday at the Kings Complex in Nausori and was attended by the High Commissioner of India to Fiji, Suneet Mehta, who officially launched the Sabha by unveiling a commemorative plaque. Minister for Employment Agni Deo Singh was also present.

Addressing members at the launch, President and Co-founder Ratnesh Kumar Bhawan said the new organisation aimed to bring fresh ideas while preserving the values of Sanatan Dharma for future generations.

“This is a new Sanatan with new ideas for our future generations,” he said.

“We want everyone’s ideas and love to move forward.”

Bhawan said the new body would encourage collective leadership and service rather than the pursuit of positions of authority.

“You must be wondering why I am standing here as the president. We have a lot of educated people with us who love Sanatan. I am here to serve and not hold a position.”

He said leadership should never become permanent or centred on individuals.

“Sometimes when we take positions, we love that too much and we refuse to leave it.”

Bhawan stressed that the new Sabha would not be afraid to embrace change or make decisions in the interests of the wider Hindu community.

“This Sanatan body is not that type of body which will be scared,” he said.

item.title: One in 60 Fijian adults now living with HIV
item.description: An estimated 1.2 per cent of Fijians aged 15 to 49 – about one in every 60 adults – are now living with HIV, as the country’s outbreak continues to escalate beyond high-risk groups into the wider community. item.content:encoded:
An estimated 1.2 per cent of Fijians aged 15 to 49 – about one in every 60 adults – are now living with HIV, as the country’s outbreak continues to escalate beyond high-risk groups into the wider community.

Speaking at the International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026), Dr Jason Mitchell, chair of Fiji’s National HIV Outbreak Cluster Response Task Force. said the country is facing one of its most serious public health crises, with HIV infections increasing 14-fold over the past five years.

He said around 12,000 people are now believed to be living with HIV in Fiji, a nation of fewer than one million people.

“In January 2025, we declared a national HIV outbreak, which was initially confined to the population of people who inject drugs. The epidemic is now spilling over into every other population group in the country,” Dr Mitchell said.

He said UNAIDS estimates HIV prevalence among people aged 15 to 49 now stands at 1.2 per cent and continues to rise.

“That’s roughly one in every 60 adults,” he said.

Dr Mitchell said the situation among pregnant women is also deteriorating, with HIV prevalence in antenatal clinics now exceeding 2 per cent.

“In 2025, one child was born with HIV every week, and we lost one child to HIV-related matters every month,” he said.

He described the situation as “the greatest crime and shame of all” because it is preventable.

The conference heard Fiji recorded the highest mother-to-child HIV transmission rate in the world last year, with about 18 per cent of HIV-positive mothers passing the virus to their babies.

Young adults continue to be the most affected, with two-thirds of new HIV diagnoses last year involving people aged between 20 and 34 years.

Dr Mitchell said 94 per cent of those diagnosed were from the iTaukei community, while infections among women continue to increase. There has also been a 45 per cent rise in HIV infections among children and teenagers aged 10 to 19.

He attributed the rapid spread of HIV among people who inject drugs to the communal sharing culture and a shortage of clean needles and syringes.

item.title: Dr Mitchell urges Fiji to fast-track new HIV prevention drug
item.description: The head of Fiji’s HIV Taskforce, Dr Jason Mitchell, has called on the country to make the long-acting HIV prevention drug lenacapavir (LEN) a central part of its response to the growing HIV epidemic. In a social media post following the International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) in Brazil, Dr Mitchell said the conference had demonstrated what could be achieved when science, political leadership an
item.content:encoded:
The head of Fiji’s HIV Taskforce, Dr Jason Mitchell, has called on the country to make the long-acting HIV prevention drug lenacapavir (LEN) a central part of its response to the growing HIV epidemic.

In a social media post following the International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) in Brazil, Dr Mitchell said the conference had demonstrated what could be achieved when science, political leadership and public health work together.

“Brazil International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) has reminded the world what is possible when science, political leadership and public health align,” he said.

Turning to Fiji’s response, Dr Mitchell said the country could no longer rely on a single prevention strategy as HIV infections continue to rise.

“We need to position long-acting lenacapavir (LEN) as a central pillar of our HIV prevention response. This is not about replacing condoms or behaviour change, it is about recognising the reality of our epidemic.”

He acknowledged that while condoms and behaviour change programmes remain important, they have not been enough to keep pace with the rapid spread of HIV.

“Condom use remains low and inconsistent. Behaviour change interventions are important, but they take time and have not kept pace with the speed at which HIV is spreading. We cannot rely on any single intervention.”

Dr Mitchell said Fiji needed a comprehensive approach centred on combination prevention.

“A generalised epidemic demands combination prevention, with biological interventions at its core.”

He said twice-yearly lenacapavir, alongside oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), condoms, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), treatment, sexually transmitted infection services and harm reduction programmes, offered an opportunity to significantly reduce new HIV infections if implemented quickly and on a large scale.

Dr Mitchell said discussions at AIDS 2026 reinforced that scientific breakthroughs would only have an impact if they were made accessible and affordable.

“Recent discussions at AIDS 2026 reinforced that breakthroughs like LEN will only change epidemics if they are made accessible, affordable and delivered to the people who need them most.”

He concluded by saying Fiji now faced a critical decision.

“The question for Fiji is no longer whether these tools work. The question is whether we have the courage and urgency to deploy them before the epidemic outpaces us again.”

item.title: ‘You are in our thoughts and prayers,’ PM tells recovering health workers
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has assured the six Ministry of Health officials injured in last week’s maritime tragedy that they remain in the thoughts and prayers of the nation as they continue their recovery. The Prime Minister visited the six officials at Twomey Hospital in Tamavua today, where they are receiving treatment following the incident in Lau waters.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has assured the six Ministry of Health officials injured in last week’s maritime tragedy that they remain in the thoughts and prayers of the nation as they continue their recovery.

The Prime Minister visited the six officials at Twomey Hospital in Tamavua today, where they are receiving treatment following the incident in Lau waters.

During the visit, he spent time with each of the recovering officials, offering words of encouragement and thanking them for their dedicated service to the people of Fiji.

Rabuka also reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to supporting the officials throughout their recovery and ensuring they receive the care and assistance they need.

Addressing the group, he said: “Vinaka vakalevu na qaravi tavi ena yalo dina, dou vakaukauwa tiko, keimami sa veinanumi tiko mai vei kemudou ena masu mo dou bulabula vinaka.”

Translated, he said: “Thank you very much for your dedicated and selfless service. Stay strong. You are in our thoughts and prayers, and we pray for your full recovery.”

The six health officials were rescued following the maritime incident in Lau waters last week and have since been receiving medical treatment in Suva.

item.title: FHRADC calls for ‘zero tolerance’ after alleged prison assault
item.description: The Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission (FHRADC) has called for zero tolerance for torture and ill-treatment following the circulation of a viral video allegedly showing a Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) officer assaulting an inmate at the Lautoka Remand Centre. In a statement, the Commission said it was concerned by the footage and welcomed the Fiji Corrections Service’s decision
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission (FHRADC) has called for zero tolerance for torture and ill-treatment following the circulation of a viral video allegedly showing a Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) officer assaulting an inmate at the Lautoka Remand Centre.

In a statement, the Commission said it was concerned by the footage and welcomed the Fiji Corrections Service’s decision to immediately launch a formal investigation into the incident.

The Commission also called for the inmate involved to receive urgent medical treatment and appropriate support while investigations continue.

“The FHRADC calls for the inmate involved to receive immediate medical attention, appropriate care and any necessary support while the investigation is underway,” the Commission said.

It reminded authorities that every person, including those held in detention, has the right to be treated with dignity and humanity.

“Individuals deprived of their liberty remain entitled to the full protection of their human rights, including freedom from all forms of torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.”

The Commission urged that the investigation be conducted promptly, independently, impartially and transparently to ensure public confidence in the outcome.

“Should the allegations be substantiated, those responsible must be held accountable in accordance with the law,” the statement said.

The FHRADC said it would continue to monitor developments and stressed that all detention facilities must uphold the highest human rights standards.

“There must be zero tolerance for torture and all forms of ill-treatment,” said FHRADC Director Loukinikini Lewaravu.

item.title: Abuse of authority not tolerated: FCS
item.description: The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has launched an investigation into an alleged assault at the Lautoka Remand Centre, saying any abuse of authority by officers will not be tolerated. The investigation follows the circulation of a video on social media showing an incident involving a prison officer and an inmate.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Corrections Service (FCS) has launched an investigation into an alleged assault at the Lautoka Remand Centre, saying any abuse of authority by officers will not be tolerated.

The investigation follows the circulation of a video on social media showing an incident involving a prison officer and an inmate.

In a statement issued today, FCS confirmed it was aware of the incident and had commissioned an investigation to establish the facts surrounding the alleged assault and determine the appropriate course of action.

“The Fiji Corrections Service also confirms that assault by an officer against a prisoner or vice versa is not tolerated and anyone found to abuse his or her authority will face the full brunt of the law,” FCS said.

The Service said the investigation would determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and any further action required.

FCS assured members of the public that a comprehensive update would be provided once the investigation had been concluded.
